Rashi on Shabbat 68b:1:1.hebrew: אבל לא שכחה - לעיקר שבת, אלא ששכח שהיום שבת — מאי:
Rashi on Shabbat 68b:1:1.english: But [if] he did not forget it - [Namely,] the essence of Shabbat, but rather he forgot that today is Shabbat — what [is the law]?

Rashi on Shabbat 68b:1:2.hebrew: חייב על כל אב מלאכה - דע"כ, אי הוה סבירא ליה דאינו חייב אלא אחת לכל שבת ושבת, הוה ליה למיכרך ולמיתני הכי: ״מי שידע עיקר שבת ושכחה, וכן היודע עיקר שבת ועשה מלאכות הרבה בשבתות הרבה — חייב על כל שבת ושבת״:
Rashi on Shabbat 68b:1:2.english: Liable for each primary labor - For perforce, if [the Tanna] held that he is liable for only one [sin-offering] for each and every Shabbat, he should have combined [them] and taught as follows: “One who knew the essence of Shabbat and forgot it, and likewise one who knows the essence of Shabbat and performed many labors on multiple Shabbatot, is liable for each and every Shabbat.”

Rashi on Shabbat 68b:1:3.hebrew: ליתני היודע עיקר שבת - דהוה שגגת שבת וזדון מלאכות הרבה, חייב על כל מלאכה, אע"ג דבכל שבת ליכא אלא חדא שגגה; וכ"ש שגגת מלאכות וזדון שבת, דאיכא שגגות הרבה:
Rashi on Shabbat 68b:1:3.english: Let [the mishna] teach: "One who knows the essence of Shabbat" - which is [a case of] unwittingness regarding Shabbat and intentionality regarding many labors, [that he is] liable for each labor, even though on each Shabbat there is only a single unwitting lapse; and all the more so [in a case of] unwittingness regarding the labors and intentionality regarding Shabbat, where there are many unwitting lapses.

Rashi on Shabbat 68b:1:4.hebrew: כהכיר ולבסוף שכח דמי - ומתניתין איצטריך למינקט הכיר ולבסוף שכח, דלא תימא חייב על כל שבת ושבת:
Rashi on Shabbat 68b:1:4.english: Is considered like one who knew and ultimately forgot - And our Mishnah needed to specify [one who] knew and ultimately forgot, so that you would not say [that] he is liable for each and every Shabbat.

Rashi on Shabbat 68b:2:1.hebrew: פטור - דקסברי רבי יוחנן ור"ל: אומר מותר — אנוס הוא, ולא שגגה היא:
Rashi on Shabbat 68b:2:1.english: Exempt - For Rabbi Yoḥanan and Reish Lakish hold: One who says [it is] permitted is [acting under] circumstances beyond his control, and it is not an unwitting transgression.

Rashi on Shabbat 68b:2:2.hebrew: וחייב על הדם - שאכל כל ימיו — אחת. וכן על כל דבר כרת שבתורה:
Rashi on Shabbat 68b:2:2.english: And he is liable for the blood - [For all the blood] that he ate all his days, [he is liable to bring only] one [sin-offering]; and similarly for every matter [punishable by] karet in the Torah.

Rashi on Shabbat 68b:3:1.hebrew: מזיד קרוי חוטא - דכתיב (ויקרא ה׳:א׳) בשבועת העדות: ״נפש כי תחטא ושמעה וגומר״, ולא כתיב ביה ״ונעלם״:
Rashi on Shabbat 68b:3:1.english: An intentional [transgressor] is called a sinner - As it is written (Leviticus 5:1) regarding the oath of testimony: “If a person sins and hears, etc.,” and it is not written regarding it: “And it was hidden [from him].”

Rashi on Shabbat 68b:3:2.hebrew: הריני מוסיף על דבריך - כלומר, אם כך באת לדרוש ג"ש ללמד שוגג ממזיד, בא ואוסיף גם אני על דבריך עוד, ובה תראה אם יעמדו דבריך:
Rashi on Shabbat 68b:3:2.english: I will add to your words - That is to say: If you have come to expound a gezeirah shavah in this manner, to learn [the law of] an unwitting [sinner] from an intentional [sinner], come, and I too will add further to your words, and through it you will see whether your words will stand.

Rashi on Shabbat 68b:3:3.english: So too, an unwitting [transgressor] who had knowledge at the time of the action - Would you obligate him in this [case] as well [to bring] a sin-offering?

Rashi on Shabbat 68b:4:1.hebrew: כ"ש שהוספת - על דברי, והרי אתה מסייעני, וגם בזו אני אומר שהוא חייב. ולקמן מפרש במאי שגג:
Rashi on Shabbat 68b:4:1.english: All the more so that you added - to my words, and behold, you are supporting me, and in this [case] as well, I say that he is liable. And later, [the Gemara] explains in what [way] he acted unwittingly.

Rashi on Shabbat 68b:5:1.hebrew: קתני מיהא - רישא, תינוק שנשבה לבין הנכרים חייב:
Rashi on Shabbat 68b:5:1.english: In any case, it taught - [In the] first clause, a child who was taken captive among the gentiles is liable.

Rashi on Shabbat 68b:5:2.hebrew: בשלמא לרב ושמואל ניחא - דאינהו נמי מחייבי, ואיכא לאוקמי דהוא הדין להכיר ולבסוף שכח כי מתניתין, וברייתא דקתני תינוק — היא גופא איצטריך לאשמעינן פלוגתא דמונבז ורבנן:
Rashi on Shabbat 68b:5:2.english: Granted, according to Rav and Shmuel it works out well - For they too hold [him] liable, and it is possible to establish that the same law applies to one who was [initially] aware and subsequently forgot, as [in] our Mishnah; and the baraita that teaches [the case of] a child — that itself was necessary to teach us the dispute between Munbaz and the Rabbis.

Rashi on Shabbat 68b:6:1.hebrew: מאי טעמא דמונבז - אבנין אב ודאי לא סמיך למיעבד שוגג דומיא דמזיד, דהאי שוגג חילוף דמזיד, וליכא לדמויינהו, דהאי חייב והאי פטור:
Rashi on Shabbat 68b:6:1.english: What is the rationale of Munbaz - He certainly did not rely on a binyan av to make an unwitting [transgressor] comparable to an intentional [transgressor], for this unwitting [transgressor] is the opposite of an intentional [transgressor], and they cannot be compared, as this one is liable and that one is exempt.

Rashi on Shabbat 68b:6:2.hebrew: מקיש שוגג - לענין חטאת, למזיד לענין כרת. ואף על גב דלא דמי, ע"כ הקישן הכתוב:
Rashi on Shabbat 68b:6:2.english: [The verse] juxtaposes [one who acts] unwittingly - with regard to a sin-offering, to [one who acts] intentionally with regard to *karet* [excision]. And even though they are not similar, perforce the verse juxtaposed them.

Rashi on Shabbat 68b:7:1.hebrew: ורבנן - הך הקישא בעיא לכדרבי יהושע ב"ל:
Rashi on Shabbat 68b:7:1.english: And the Rabbis - That juxtaposition is needed for that [teaching] of Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi.

Rashi on Shabbat 68b:7:2.hebrew: תורה אחת יהיה לכם - גבי קרבן ע"ז כתיב בפרשת שלח לך אנשים:
Rashi on Shabbat 68b:7:2.english: There shall be one law for you - It is written regarding the offering for idolatry in the portion of Shelach Lekha Anashim:

Tosafot on Shabbat 68b:1:1.hebrew: אבל לא שכחה מאי חייב על כל מלאכה ומלאכה - תימה לר"י: מנא ליה למידק הכי? אימא: דלא שכחה נמי אינו חייב על כל מלאכה ומלאכה, אלא על כל שבת ושבת כמו בהכיר ולבסוף שכח, ותנא הכיר ולבסוף שכח, וכ"ש הא, כדפרי'! ומה שפי' בקונטרס, דדייק דחייב על כל מלאכה ומלאכה מדלא כייל להו אהדדי: "מי שידע עיקר שבת ושכחה, והיודע עיקר שבת, חייב על כל שבת ושבת", דהוה משמע דוקא על כל שבת ושבת ולא על כל מלאכה — אין נראה לר"י; דא"כ, היכי פריך לעיל: "לתני הכיר ולבסוף שכח, וכל שכן הא", דמשמע דהא לא איצטריך למיתני, והא נמי איצטריך לאשמעינן דאינו חייב על כל מלאכה ומלאכה! ונראה לר"י, דלעיל דקאמר: "ליתני הכיר ולבסוף שכח, וכ"ש הא", לא בעי למימר דלא ליתני' כלל במשנה; אלא ה"פ: מדקתני "חייב על כל שבת ושבת", ולא קתני "אינו חייב אלא על כל שבת", דהוה משמע ולא על כל מלאכה ומלאכה, משמע דעיקר מתניתין חיובא אתא לאשמעינן, דחייב על כל שבת ושבת, ולא פטורא דאינו חייב על כל מלאכה. ואם כן, ליתני "הכיר ולבסוף שכח", דהוי רבותא טפי, וכ"ש האי דחייב על כל שבת, ולא הוה צריך למתנייה בהאי בבא; אלא ה"ל למיתני בתר הכי בבבא אחריתי: "היודע עיקר שבת אינו חייב אלא על כל שבת ושבת", לאשמעינן דאינו חייב על כל מלאכה. והשתא דייק שפיר: אבל לא שכחה מאי — חייב על כל מלאכה ומלאכה, מדלא תני בבבא אחריתי דאינו חייב אלא על כל שבת ושבת:
Tosafot on Shabbat 68b:1:1.english: "But if he did not forget, what [is the law]? He is liable for each and every labor" - Ri finds this puzzling: From where did [the Gemara] infer this? Say [instead] that even if he did not forget [the essence of Shabbat], he is also not liable for each and every labor, but rather for each and every Shabbat, just like in the case of one who knew and ultimately forgot; and [the Mishnah] taught "one who knew and ultimately forgot," and all the more so this [case of knowing the essence of Shabbat], as we explained! And that which [Rashi] explained in the Kuntres — that [the Gemara] inferred that he is liable for each and every labor from the fact that [the Mishnah] did not group them together: "One who knew the essence of Shabbat and forgot it, and one who knows the essence of Shabbat, are liable for each and every Shabbat," which would have indicated specifically for each and every Shabbat and not for each labor — this does not appear [correct] to Ri; for if so, how did [the Gemara] object above: "Let [the Mishnah] teach 'one who knew and ultimately forgot,' and all the more so this [case]" — which implies that this [case] did not need to be taught, yet this [case] was also needed, to teach us that he is not liable for each and every labor! And it appears to Ri that above, when [the Gemara] said: "Let it teach 'one who knew and ultimately forgot,' and all the more so this [case]," it did not mean to say that it should not teach it at all in the Mishnah; rather, this is the explanation: Since it teaches "he is liable for each and every Shabbat," and does not teach "he is liable only for each Shabbat," which would have implied "and not for each and every labor," this indicates that the primary purpose of our Mishnah was to teach an obligation — that he is liable for each and every Shabbat — and not an exemption, [namely] that he is not liable for each labor. And if so, let it teach "one who knew and ultimately forgot," which is a greater novelty, and all the more so this [one who did not forget] is liable for each Shabbat, and there would have been no need to teach him in this clause; rather, it should have taught afterward in a separate clause: "One who knows the essence of Shabbat is liable only for each and every Shabbat," to teach us that he is not liable for each labor. And now, [the Gemara] accurately infers: "But if he did not forget, what [is the law]? He is liable for each and every labor" — from the fact that it did not teach in a separate clause that he is liable only for each and every Shabbat.

Tosafot on Shabbat 68b:1:2.hebrew: ליתני היודע עיקר שבת וכ"ש הא - תימה לר"י: לרבא, דאמר בכריתות בסוף פרק אמרו לו (כריתות דף טז:) דבזדון שבת ושגגת מלאכות לא מיחייב אכל שבת ושבת, ודייק ממתניתין דהכא דלא קתני "חייב על כל אב מלאכה ומלאכה של כל שבת ושבת" — ולדידיה, היכי פריך הכא: "ליתני היודע עיקר שבת"? הא לא מצי למיתני הכי, דאם כן הוה משמע דלא מיחייב היודע עיקר שבת אכל שבת ושבת! ותירץ: דהכי פריך — דליתני: "היודע עיקר שבת, דחייב אכל אב מלאכה של כל שבת ושבת". ורשב"א מפרש: דאי הוה תני בהדיא "היודע עיקר שבת חייב על כל אב מלאכה", ליכא למידק דלא מיחייב אכל שבת מדלא קתני "חייב על כל אב מלאכה של כל שבת"; דלא צריך למיתני', דמרישא שמעינן ליה, דקתני בהכיר ולבסוף שכח דחייב על כל שבת ושבת, כ"ש יודע עיקר שבת כדאמר לעיל:
Tosafot on Shabbat 68b:1:2.english:
"Let it teach: 'One who knows the essence of Shabbat,' and all the more so this" - The Ri raises a difficulty: According to Rava, who said in Keritot at the end of the chapter [entitled] Amru Lo (16b) that in [a case of] intentional [awareness of] Shabbat and unwitting [transgression of prohibited] labors, one is not liable for each and every Shabbat, and he deduced [this] from our mishna here, which does not teach: "He is liable for each and every primary category of labor of each and every Shabbat" — according to him, how can [the Gemara] object here: "Let [the mishna] teach: 'One who knows the essence of Shabbat'"? But [the mishna] could not have taught this, for if so, it would have implied that one who knows the essence of Shabbat is not liable for each and every Shabbat!
And he resolved [it]: This is what [the Gemara] is asking — let [the mishna] teach: "One who knows the essence of Shabbat [is] liable for each primary category of labor of each and every Shabbat."
And Rashba explains: If [the mishna] had explicitly taught: "One who knows the essence of Shabbat is liable for each primary category of labor," one could not deduce that he is not liable for each Shabbat from [the fact] that it did not teach: "He is liable for each primary category of labor of each Shabbat." For it would not have needed to teach it, since we learn it from the first clause, which taught regarding one who knew and ultimately forgot that he is liable for each and every Shabbat — all the more so one who knows the essence of Shabbat, as [the Gemara] stated above.

Tosafot on Shabbat 68b:1:3.hebrew: וכ"ש האי - ה"נ לא בעי למימר דלא לתני' כלל במשנה, דאם כן, הוה אמינא דחייב נמי על כל שבת ושבת, ואינו כן לרבה דכריתות. אלא ליתני בבא אחריתי: "היודע שהוא שבת אינו חייב על כל שבת":
Tosafot on Shabbat 68b:1:3.english: "And all the more so this one" - Here too, [the Gemara] does not mean to say that [the Mishnah] should not teach it at all, for if so, one would say that he is liable also for each and every Shabbat, and that is not so according to Rabba in [tractate] Keritot. Rather, let it teach another clause: "One who knows that it is Shabbat is not liable for each Shabbat."

Tosafot on Shabbat 68b:1:4.hebrew: כי הכיר ולבסוף שכח דמי - פירש בקונטרס, דלהכי לא תנא במתניתין שכח מעיקרו — דהיינו תינוק שנשבה — דלא תימא דהכיר ולבסוף שכח חייב על כל שבת. וקשה לר"י: דמ"מ ליתנייה, וליתני נמי בתר הכי: "הכיר ולבסוף שכח אינו חייב אלא אחת", דכה"ג פריך לעיל: "ליתני הכיר ולבסוף שכח, וכ"ש הא", כדפרישית. ונראה לר"י, דודאי אי הוה תני "חייב חטאת" — דהוה אתי לאשמעינן חיובא — הוה שייך למיפרך: דליתני תינוק שנשבה, דהוי רבותא טפי; אבל השתא דקתני "אינו חייב אלא אחת" — דפטורה אתא לאשמעינן — נקט "הכיר ולבסוף שכח", דהוי רבותא טפי. ומיהו קשה לר"י: דמ"מ ליתני תינוק שנשבה, דלא נטעה לומר דפטור כרבי יוחנן וריש לקיש, והדר ליתני הכיר ולבסוף שכח:
Tosafot on Shabbat 68b:1:4.english: Has the status of one who knew and ultimately forgot - Rashi explained that this is why the Mishnah did not teach [the case of one who] forgot from the outset, that is, a child taken captive [among gentiles]: so that you would not say that one who knew and ultimately forgot is liable for each Shabbat. And this is difficult to the Ri: For nevertheless, let [the Mishnah] teach it, and let it also teach afterward: "One who knew and ultimately forgot is liable for only one [offering]"? For in this manner [the Gemara] asked above: "Let it teach 'one who knew and ultimately forgot,' and all the more so this one," as I explained. And it appears to the Ri that certainly if [the Mishnah] had taught "is liable for a sin-offering" — where it would have come to teach liability — it would have been appropriate to ask: Let it teach [the case of] a captive child, which is a greater novelty; but now that it teaches "is liable for only one [offering]" — where it came to teach an exemption — it formulated [the case of] "one who knew and ultimately forgot," which is a greater novelty. However, it is difficult to the Ri: For nevertheless, let it teach [the case of] a captive child so that we would not mistakenly say that he is exempt, like Rabbi Yochanan and Reish Lakish, and then let it teach "one who knew and ultimately forgot."

Tosafot on Shabbat 68b:2:1.hebrew: אבל תינוק שנשבה פטור - פירש בקונטרס דקסברי: אומר מותר — אנוס הוא. ואין נראה, דטעמייהו כמונבז, כדאמר בסמוך, וטעמא דמונבז מפרש לקמן דיליף מקרא. והא דאמר בפ"ב דמכות (דף ז:) גבי גלות: "בשגגה" — פרט למזיד, ומפרש (אביי) [צ"ל רבא]: פרט לאומר מותר, ופריך ליה (רבא) [צ"ל אביי]: אומר מותר אנוס הוא — לאו דוקא קאמר אנוס, דבכל מקום מחייבין ליה, אלא לגבי גלות דוקא ממעט (אביי) [צ"ל רבא] אומר מותר, משום דטובא "בשגגה" כתיב התם; דהא בפירקין מחייבי אומר מותר בע"ז ובחלב, אע"ג דכתיב בהן "בשגגה". (ורבא) [צ"ל ואביי] פריך ליה: אומר מותר אנוס הוא, ולא הוה ליה למיתני בברייתא "בשגגה פרט למזיד", אלא פרט לאנוס, דיותר דמי וקרוב לאנוס מלמזיד:
Tosafot on Shabbat 68b:2:1.english: However, a child who was taken captive is exempt - Rashi explained that they hold [that] one who says "[this prohibited act] is permitted" is [considered] a victim of circumstance beyond his control (anuss). But this does not appear [correct], for their reason is like Munbaz, as [the Gemara] says nearby; and the reason of Munbaz is explained below (69a), that he derives it from a verse. And as for that which [the Gemara] says in the second chapter of Makkot (7b) regarding exile: "[He who kills his fellow] unwittingly" (Deuteronomy 19:4) — to exclude one who acts intentionally; and (Abaye) [it should say: Rava] explains: To exclude one who says "[it is] permitted"; and (Rava) [it should say: Abaye] objects to him: One who says "[it is] permitted" is an anuss — [Abaye] did not mean strictly [that he is an] anuss, for in all [other] places they obligate him; rather, regarding exile specifically does (Abaye) [it should say: Rava] exclude one who says "[it is] permitted," because "unwittingly" is written many times there; for in our chapter, they obligate one who says "[it is] permitted" in [the cases of] idolatry and [forbidden] fat, even though "unwittingly" is written regarding them. And (and Rava) [it should say: and Abaye] objects to him: "One who says '[it is] permitted' is an anuss" — and the baraita should not have taught "'unwittingly' excludes an intentional actor," but rather "excludes an anuss," for he is more similar and closer to an anuss than to an intentional actor.

Tosafot on Shabbat 68b:2:2.hebrew: וחייב על הדם אחת - אע"ג דמילתא דפשיטא היא, דאכל מה שאכל דם אינו חייב אלא אחת, כיון שאין בדם חילוק איסור כמו שיש בשבת חילוק מלאכות, וכל אדם נמי בלא תינוק שנשבה אכל דם ודם אינו חייב אלא אחת — אלא אומר ר"י דמיירי דאפי' אכלן בכמה תמחויין, דלר"י (לקמן שבת דף עא.) אדם אחר חייב על כל תמחוי אפי' בהעלם אחד, ובתינוק שנשבה אינו חייב אלא אחד. אך קשה לרשב"א: דמאי איצטריך תו לאשמעינן ולמתני "ועל החלב אחד":
Tosafot on Shabbat 68b:2:2.english: "And he is liable for the blood, one" - Even though it is an obvious matter that for whatever blood he ate, he is only liable [to bring] one [sin-offering], since with blood there is no division of the prohibition as there is on Shabbat with the division of labors, and any person as well, not [just] a captive child, [who] ate blood and [more] blood is only liable [to bring] one [sin-offering] — rather, the Ri says that [the baraita] is dealing [with a case where] he even ate them from several dishes, for according to Rabbi Yehoshua (below, Shabbat 71a), another person is liable for each dish even in a single lapse of awareness, whereas in [the case of] a captive child he is only liable [to bring] one. However, the Rashba raises a difficulty: Why was it further necessary to teach us and to state, "and for the forbidden fat, one"?

Tosafot on Shabbat 68b:4:1.hebrew: כל שכן שהוספת - כדפירש בקונטרס, דאף בזו מחייב, ומחייב נמי כי ליכא ידיעה בשעת מעשה — דהא רבי יוחנן וריש לקיש סברי כמונבז, ומחייבי הכיר ולבסוף שכח; ותניא נמי לקמן: "שגג בזה ובזה — זהו שוגג האמור בתורה", ומוקמינן לה כמונבז. והיינו טעמא — משום דסברא הוא דלא איתקש שוגג למזיד לאפוקי ליה ממשמעות שגגה; דאדרבה, שוגג משמע דלית ליה ידיעה בשעת מעשה, ולא אתא היקשא אלא לחייב נמי כי אית ליה ידיעה בשעת מעשה. ומיהו קשה לר"י: דהא פטרי מהיקשא תינוק שנשבה — מהאי טעמא נמי יפטור הכיר ולבסוף שכח:
Tosafot on Shabbat 68b:4:1.english: "All the more so that you have elaborated" - As explained in the Kuntres [Rashi], that [Munbaz] deems [one] liable even in this [case], and he also deems [one] liable when there is no awareness at the time of the action — for Rabbi Yoḥanan and Reish Lakish hold in accordance with Munbaz, and they deem liable one who knew and subsequently forgot; and it is also taught below: "If one acted unwittingly with regard to both this and that, that is the unwitting sinner mentioned in the Torah," and we establish [the baraita] in accordance with Munbaz. And this is the rationale — because it is logical that an unwitting sinner was not juxtaposed to an intentional sinner to exclude him from the [plain] meaning of "unwitting"; for on the contrary, "unwitting" implies that he does not have awareness at the time of the action, and the juxtaposition came only to deem [one] liable also when he does have awareness at the time of the action. However, this is difficult to the Ri: for behold, they exempt a child taken captive based on the juxtaposition; by this same reasoning, he should also exempt one who knew and subsequently forgot!
